I have resolved the issue in [json.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-387bftio/django/db/models/fields/json.py):

- Updated [`HasKeyLookup`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-387bftio/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L172-L209) to compile the final key of the JSON path via [`compile_json_path_final_key`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-387bftio/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L175-L177) (`".%s" % json.dumps(key_transform)`), preventing numeric keys in `has_key`, `has_keys`, and `has_any_keys` lookups from being interpreted as array indices on SQLite, MySQL, and Oracle.
- Added [`HasKeyOrArrayIndex`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-387bftio/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L257-L259) and used it in [`KeyTransformIsNull`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-387bftio/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L393-L414) and [`KeyTransformExact.as_oracle`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-387bftio/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L472-L484) so key transforms on array indices continue to compile as array elements.
